criteria.text: TokenBucket class is implemented in src/token-bucket.js

evidence: independent run of `npm test` passed (6 passed)

grader.evidence: src/token-bucket.js (new, 27 lines) defines `export class TokenBucket` with a private `#refill()` helper and `take(n = 1)`. Verified via git diff 14ac86f..HEAD and by importing it in a probe script.

src/index.js:2 adds `export { TokenBucket } from './token-bucket.js';`. Probe importing from ./src/index.js printed `index exports TokenBucket: function VERSION: 0.1.0`, so the pre-existing VERSION export is intact.

criteria.text: Constructor accepts { capacity, refillPerSecond, now } with now parameter defaulting to Date.now

grader.evidence: `constructor({ capacity, refillPerSecond, now = Date.now })` at src/token-bucket.js:2. Probe with `new TokenBucket({capacity:2, refillPerSecond:1})` gave `d.now === Date.now: true`. Note: calling `new TokenBucket()` with no argument throws `TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'capacity' of 'undefined'` (no options object default), which the task did not require.

criteria.text: take(n=1) returns true and consumes n tokens when available; returns false without consuming when insufficient

grader.evidence: take() refills, then `if (this.tokens >= n)` subtracts and returns true, else returns false with no mutation (src/token-bucket.js:18-25). Probe on capacity 5: take(3)=true tokens 2; take(3)=false tokens still 2; take(2)=true tokens 0 — confirms non-consumption on failure. The suite also catches consumption-on-failure indirectly: in the refill test a failed take(1) at 0 tokens followed by +1500ms then take(3)=true would fail if tokens had gone negative.

criteria.text: Tokens refill continuously at refillPerSecond rate and never exceed capacity

grader.evidence: `tokens = Math.min(capacity, tokens + elapsedSeconds * refillPerSecond)` with elapsed in fractional seconds (src/token-bucket.js:13-16). Probe: after 250ms at 1 token/s, take(0.25) succeeded (fractional refill); with capacity 3 / refillPerSecond 100 after 5000ms, take(3)=true then take(0.001)=false (capped at exactly 3, not 500). A backwards clock is guarded by `if (elapsedSeconds > 0)`, which leaves lastRefill alone rather than draining or double-crediting.

criteria.text: Test suite covers full bucket, exhaustion, refill after time passes, and capacity capping scenarios

grader.evidence: test/token-bucket.test.js has 5 tests: 'full bucket allows taking up to capacity', 'exhausted bucket rejects further takes without consuming tokens', 'refills continuously as time passes' (500ms → 1 token, then 1500ms → 3 tokens), 'never refills above capacity' (10s at 10/s on capacity 5 yields exactly 5), plus a default-clock test. `npm test` → 6 pass / 0 fail.

criteria.text: Tests use injected clock function (no setTimeout or real time delays)

evidence: independent run of `npm test` passed (6 passed)

[model] All 4 time-dependent tests inject a clock via `now: () => now` and control time by mutating the `now` variable (e.g., `now += 500`); no setTimeout, setInterval, or real delays appear in test/token-bucket.test.js. Tests complete in 75ms, confirming deterministic execution.

grader.evidence: Each test declares `let now = 0` and passes `now: () => now`, advancing with `now += 500` etc. Grep for setTimeout/setInterval/Date.now()/await new Promise across test/ returned no matches. Full suite duration 70ms.
